card: Enables the -Wmissing-noreturn compiler warning flag in CMake and annotates non-returning functions, methods, and lambdas across the codebase with [[noreturn]]. It also qualifies bare C runtime abort and exit calls with std:: and suppresses the warning around fuzz harness initializers whose return behaviour depends on build configuration. This prevents compiler false positives, such as spurious missing-return warnings, where the compiler cannot determine that an execution branch unconditionally terminates.
changed_since_previous: Dropped suppression of Clang's -Wc++23-lambda-attributes warning on annotated lambdas.
evidence: Description notes: "Missing [[noreturn]] attributes can cause compiler false positives and other issues; see discussion in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35896#discussion_r3726612556."
problem: Functions that never return lack [[noreturn]] annotations, which can cause compiler analysis false positives such as spurious missing-return warnings. Without an enforced compiler warning flag, newly added non-returning functions easily omit the attribute.

risk.why: Incorrectly marking a function as non-returning when it could return causes undefined behavior, but all annotated functions unconditionally throw or call abort/exit.

scope_notes: Touches non-returning stubs and exit handlers across many subsystems (fuzzing, tests, GUI, validation, sync), replacing unreachable returns in mock sockets with std::abort().
summary: Enables the -Wmissing-noreturn compiler warning flag in CMake and adds missing [[noreturn]] attributes to functions, methods, and lambdas that unconditionally exit or throw. It also replaces bare C abort(), exit(), and _Exit() calls with std:: namespace qualifications from <cstdlib>, and pragmas out the warning in the fuzz harness where return behaviour is build-dependent.
